title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance and Manager Guide
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's standard processes for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and engineering and product managers who onboard and coach individual contributors. The guidance below balances consistency and speed while protecting candidate and employee experience, legal/compliance requirements, and fairness.

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time, part-time, and contractor hires in engineering, product, research, customer-facing, and corporate functions.
- Includes steps from req creation through the candidate offer, new-hire onboarding (Day 0-90), and regular performance cycles.

1) Hiring: end-to-end process (high level)

Purpose: hire for capability, mission-fit, and long-term potential while maintaining fairness and speed.

Steps: 
1. Requisition creation and approval
   - Manager drafts JD using role template and posts a requisition in Greenhouse. JD must include core responsibilities, must-have skills, and salary band.
   - People Ops reviews for compensation banding, EO language, and headcount capacity. Approval target: 3 business days.
2. Sourcing and screening
   - Sourcing channels: internal referrals, job board postings, targeted outreach, and recruiting agencies (pre-approved list).
   - Recruiter performs resume screen and 15-30 minute phone screen to confirm base qualification and interest. Screeners use the standard phone-screen checklist (linked).
3. Interview loop design and scheduling
   - Typical loop for engineering: take-home (optional) or live coding -> technical deep-dive -> systems/design -> manager interview -> cross-functional/culture interview -> bar-raiser/peer interview. Total loop target: 2-4 interviews, completed within 10 business days.
   - Interview rubrics and scorecards must be used for every stage.
4. Decision and calibration
   - Hiring manager consolidates feedback within 48 hours of last interview and selects top candidate(s).
   - For senior roles (Director+), panel calibration with Hiring Committee required (see Decision Record 2025-03: Senior Hiring).
5. Offer and negotiation
   - People Ops prepares offer package (comp, equity outline, benefits summary). Manager confirms role and start date.
   - Target offer turnaround: 24-48 hours after verbal approval. Negotiation policy: refer to pay-bands and escalation to People Ops lead for exceptions.
6. Background checks and eligibility
   - Conditional offer pending background check and reference checks. For regulated roles, additional compliance checks may be required.

Interview Guidelines and Scoring:
- Use structured rubrics (technical competency, problem solving, communication, ownership, role-specific skills).
- Scores: 1 (Insufficient) to 5 (Exceptional). Hiring decisions require average >= 3.5 unless explicit justification documented.

Scorecard example (table):
| Dimension | 1 - Insufficient | 3 - Meets expectations | 5 - Exceptional |
|-----------|------------------|------------------------|-----------------|
| Problem Solving | Fails to decompose problems | Applies standard patterns with minor gaps | Identifies novel approaches and tradeoffs |
| System Design | Poor architecture | Correct baselines and tradeoffs | Elegant, scalable design with clear constraints |
| Communication | Unclear, frequent confusion | Clear, concise, responsive | Influences cross-functional decisions |

Diversity & fairness checklist:
- Use diverse interview panels where possible.
- Avoid asking illegal questions (age, family, disability, immigration status).
- Provide accommodations on request; candidate has option to tell recruiter.

2) Offer approvals and compensation bands

- All offers must map to the published compensation bands for the role and location.
- Manager proposes level and comp within band. People Ops approves final OTE and equity grants.
- For exceptions > 10% above band midpoint, written approval from Director of People Ops required.

3) New-hire onboarding: Day 0-90 (checklist and milestones)

Overview: Onboarding goal is to make new hires productive, socially integrated, and confident in role and tools within 90 days. The onboarding program includes pre-boarding, Day 1, Week 1, Month 1, and 30/60/90 checkpoints.

Pre-boarding (1-14 days before start)
- People Ops sends welcome packet: offer letter, benefits summary, access instructions, pre-boarding checklist, and equipment form.
- Manager confirms first-week schedule and assigns a buddy.
- IT provision request initiated (laptop, access, VPN, KMS access if needed for private deployments).

Day 1
- Orientation (People Ops): company mission, org chart, handbook overview, security training, acceptable use policy.
- Team welcome: manager meets >1 hour to review role, expectations, immediate priorities.
- Access verification: Slack, email, internal Confluence, Git repos, CI/CD dashboards.

Week 1 checklist
- Complete required training (security, privacy, code of conduct).
- Team onboarding meetings: architecture overview, product context, first project plan.
- Set 30/60/90 goals with manager.

Month 1 (30-day checkpoint)
- Manager + new hire 30-minute checkpoint: progress on goals, blockers, feedback on onboarding.
- Buddy feedback: buddy shares observations to manager/People Ops for continuous improvement.

Month 2 (60-day checkpoint)
- Ensure contributor is shipping small scoped work and participating in team rituals.

Month 3 (90-day review)
- Formal 90-day review: manager documents performance vs goals, provides rating (meets/needs improvement/exceeds), and establishes next milestones. People Ops records outcome and updates employee profile.

Onboarding templates and artifacts (links):
- New Hire 90-Day Plan (template)
- Buddy checklist
- IT access runbook

4) Performance and feedback cycles

Cycle cadence:
- Continuous feedback: encouraged weekly 1:1s and real-time feedback in peer reviews.
- Formal cycles: Quarterly check-ins (informal written notes) and annual performance review + calibration.
- Promotion and leveling cycles handled semi-annually with calibration meetings for roles and bands.

Quarterly check-ins:
- Manager documents progress against goals, development needs, and career conversations.
- Employees submit a short self-assessment (2-4 bullet highlights) prior to the check-in.

Annual review process (timeline):
1. Goal refresh (Q4): manager and employee set priorities for next year.
2. Self-assessment (Jan): employees complete self-assessment form in the People Ops system.
3. Manager assessment (Feb): manager prepares narrative and rating supported by evidence (PRs, projects, peer feedback).
4. Calibration (late Feb): cross-functional calibration panel ensures leveling consistency and fairness.
5. Compensation & rewards (Mar): People Ops finalizes merit increases and equity refreshes per budget guidance.

Ratings and calibration:
- Rating scale: Needs Improvement | Meets Expectations | Exceeds Expectations | Outstanding.
- Calibration requires documentation for any rating of Exceeds or Outstanding.
- Appeals: employees may request a review with manager and People Ops within 14 days of formal rating notification.

Career conversations and growth plans:
- Managers must have documented career discussions at least twice per year.
- Growth plans include skill milestones, stretch projects, mentorship, and expected timeline to next level.
- People Ops maintains leveling guides and role profiles.

5) Promotion and role changes

- Promotion packet: manager assembles evidence (projects, impact metrics, peer feedback, customer outcomes) and recommends new level and comp.
- Promotion approvals: manager -> Director -> People Ops -> VP (depending on level).
- Timing: typical promotion timeline is >12 months in current level unless exceptional impact justifies acceleration.

6) Manager responsibilities (short checklist)
- Recruiting: own candidate experience and ensure timely feedback.
- Onboarding: create first-week schedule, assign buddy, set 30/60/90 plan.
- Performance: weekly 1:1s, quarterly check-ins, annual reviews, documentation of feedback.
- Career development: run calibration-ready promotion packets and support learning budgets.
- Compliance: ensure completion of mandatory trainings and access reviews.

7) Offboarding and role transitions
- Manager initiates offboarding request in People Ops portal and notifies IT/security.
- Exit checklist: revoke access, complete knowledge transfer, conduct exit interview, and document lessons learned.

8) Templates and playbooks (links and location)
- Role template library: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates
- Interview rubrics and scorecards: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness
- Onboarding assets: /confluence/company-handbook/onboarding-templates
- Promotion & compensation process: /confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: People Ops (Ava Martinez) - overall policy and program updates.
- Managers: day-to-day execution and candidate experience.
- Recruiting: owns speed-to-hire metrics and pipeline health.
- For disputes or salary exceptions, escalate to Director of People Ops (Priya Patel).

Metrics and targets (People Ops dashboard):
- Time to fill (requisition open -> accepted): target <= 45 days.
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 70%.
- New hire 90-day retention: target >= 95%.
- Hiring panel diversity: target >= 30% underrepresented representation on panels.

Document maintenance:
- Review cadence: annual review or sooner if policy/regulation changes.
- Last substantive review: 2026-02-20 (people-ops).

Appendix: Quick checklists
- Hiring quick checklist: create requisition -> phone screen -> schedule loop -> candidate decision -> offer -> background check.
- Day 1 checklist: orientation, manager meet, tool access check, buddy intro.
- 90-day review items: goals, impact examples, manager rating, next steps.

End of document.
